Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $\bar g$
be a smooth background metric with Levi-Civita connection $\bar\nabla$, and let
$H^a=g^{bc}(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc})$ be the harmonic-gauge vector
of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Then:

**(a) [principal part]** Let $\hat g$ be a smooth Lorentzian metric on an open
set $U\subseteq M$ and let $h$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on
$U$. The derivative at $\hat g$ in the direction $h$ of the operator
$g\mapsto\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}[g]-\bar\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}[g]$ equals
$$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\,\bar\nabla_c\bar\nabla_d h_{ab}+L_{ab}(h,\bar\nabla h;\hat g,\bar g),$$
where $L$ is a smooth expression linear in $h$ and its first
$\bar\nabla$-derivatives with coefficients built from $\hat g,\hat g^{-1}$, its first and second
$\bar\nabla$-derivatives, $\bar g$ and the background curvature. Thus the
coefficients depend on the full second jet of the linearization metric. In particular the principal symbol is
$-\tfrac12\hat g^{cd}\xi_c\xi_d$ times the identity on the metric slot at every
covector $\xi$.

**(b) [first-order reduction]** Fix constants $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and a prescribed smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on the chart domain. Fix a chart $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with
$x^0=t$. Introduce the metric variables
$$u:=\bigl(g_{ab},\ p_{ab}:=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab},\ q_{abi}:=\bar\nabla_ig_{ab}\bigr)$$
(symmetry in $a,b$ understood) and the relation variables $\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}-p_{ab}=0$ and $\bar\nabla_0q_{abi}-\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}=\mathcal C_{abi}$, where $\mathcal C_{abi}=-\bar R^c{}_{a0i}g_{cb}-\bar R^c{}_{b0i}g_{ac}$. Then the reduced Einstein equation can be solved for the second time derivatives in the form
$$\bar\nabla_0p_{ab}=-(g^{00})^{-1}\Bigl[2g^{0i}\bar\nabla_ip_{ab}+g^{ij}\bar\nabla_iq_{abj}+R_{ab}(x,u,T;\kappa,\Lambda,\bar g)\Bigr],$$
where the source is smooth in the first-order metric state and the prescribed matter data, with no derivatives of $T$, and includes $2\kappa(T_{ab}-\tfrac12(g^{cd}T_{cd})g_{ab})+2\Lambda g_{ab}$. The resulting first-order system for $u$ is symmetric hyperbolic on every
region where $g^{00}<0$ and the spatial block $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite:
the coefficient of $\bar\nabla_0u$ is the block diagonal
$\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ (on the three slots
$g,p,q$), which is positive definite there, and the coefficients of the spatial
derivatives are symmetric. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

$\bar g$ with Levi-Civita connection $\bar\nabla$
([[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), whose Christoffel

([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

**(a) Gauge vector.** The **harmonic-gauge vector field** of the pair
$(g,\bar g)$ is the smooth vector field
$$H^a:=g^{bc}\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\bigr) .$$
The difference of the connection coefficients is a $(1,2)$-tensor, so $H$ is a
well-defined smooth vector field independent of the chart used to express the
symbols ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).

pair $(g,T)$ with respect to $\bar g$ is the second-order quasilinear system
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}=\kappa\bigl(T_{ab}-\tfrac12Tg_{ab}\bigr)+\Lambda g_{ab},$$
where $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ is the Ricci tensor of $g$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]),
$H_b=g_{bc}H^c$ and $\nabla_{(a}H_{b)}=\tfrac12(\nabla_aH_b+\nabla_bH_a)$.

**(c) Reduced solutions.** A **reduced solution** on $U$ is a pair $(g,T)$ of a
smooth Lorentzian metric and a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor on $U$ satisfying
(b) for the fixed background $\bar g$.

**(d) Einstein residual.** The **Einstein residual** of a pair $(g,T)$ is the
smooth symmetric $2$-tensor
$$E_{ab}:=G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa T_{ab},\qquad G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Sg_{ab},$$

([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). The pair solves the Einstein

[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]].

[[thm-gr-harmonic-constraint-propagation]].

Let $U\subseteq M$ be an open set with smooth observer congruence $n$, let $F$ be a smooth real two-form on $U$, and let $c>0$ be the coordinate conversion parameter of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Define covectors

$$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b,\qquad B_a:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b.$$

Here $c$ is the positive coordinate-conversion parameter of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with SI unit $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ in its length-coordinate convention. The names electric and magnetic distinguish these two covectors; for arbitrary mathematical $F$ no physical field unit or measurement is assigned.

For each $p\in U$, define the **rest covector space** by

$$\mathcal R^*_{n,p}:=\{\alpha\in T_p^*M:\alpha(n_p)=0\}.$$

The musical isomorphism $\flat_p$ maps the vector rest space $n_p^\perp$ onto $\mathcal R^*_{n,p}$: $\alpha\in\mathcal R^*_{n,p}$ iff $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,n_p)=\alpha(n_p)=0$. Moreover, $g_p^{-1}(v^\flat,w^\flat)=g_p(v,w)$, so the restriction of $g_p^{-1}$ to $\mathcal R^*_{n,p}$ is positive definite by [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]. The covectors $E_p$ and $B_p$ annihilate $n_p$; define $\langle E,B\rangle_n(p):=g_p^{-1}(E_p,B_p)$. Then

$$F=n^\flat\wedge E/c+\star_g(n^\flat\wedge B),$$

$$F_{ab}F^{ab}=2\bigl(\langle B,B\rangle_n-\langle E,E\rangle_n/c^2\bigr),\qquad F\wedge F=-\frac{2}{c}\langle E,B\rangle_n\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Equivalently, in any positively oriented future tetrad with $E_0=n$, and with $\epsilon_{123}=+1$ in its oriented spatial triad, the components satisfy $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. These are pointwise mathematical decompositions of an arbitrary two-form; no Maxwell equation or physical observation is assumed.
$$({\star_gF})_{ab}=\frac12(\mathrm{vol}_g)_{abcd}F^{cd}.$$
The **Riemannian divergence** is defined in a local orientation by $\mathcal L_X\operatorname{vol}_g=(\operatorname{div}_gX)\operatorname{vol}_g$.
In coordinates, $\operatorname{div}_gX=(\det G)^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\partial_i((\det G)^{1/2}X^i)$.

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R\times\Sigma$ be a coordinate neighborhood in an oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, foliated by spacelike $s$-levels. Write
$$g=-\alpha^2ds^2+h_{ij}(dx^i+\beta^i ds)(dx^j+\beta^j ds),\qquad \alpha>0,\qquad h=(h_{ij})>0,$$
and let $n=\alpha^{-1}(\partial_s-\beta^i\partial_i)$ be the future unit normal. On a smaller neighborhood choose a positively oriented orthonormal spatial frame $(\mathsf e_1,\mathsf e_2,\mathsf e_3)$ by Gram–Schmidt. Let $D$ be the Levi-Civita derivative of $h$, define $\operatorname{div}_h v:=D_iv^i$ and $(\operatorname{curl}_h v)_i:=\epsilon_i{}^{jk}D_jv_k$, and define the spatial cross product by $(u\times v)_i=\epsilon_{ijk}u_jv_k$ in this frame. For a smooth real two-form $F$, define the real spatial components $e_i:=F(\mathsf e_i,n)$ and $b_i:=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathsf e_j,\mathsf e_k)$, with $\epsilon_{123}=1$; thus $F_{0i}=-e_i$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$ in the adapted tetrad. Assume the source-free model of draft definition [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], whose actual equations are $dF=0$ and $d\star_gF=0$; its draft status and manifest omission are recorded in [L1].

The six evolution equations for $(e,b)$ have principal part
$$n(e)-\operatorname{curl}_h b=\text{terms with no derivatives of }(e,b),\qquad n(b)+\operatorname{curl}_h e=\text{terms with no derivatives of }(e,b).$$
For a spatial covector $\xi$, let $C(\xi)v:=\xi^\sharp\times v$ in the oriented orthonormal frame. Set $\theta^0:=\alpha ds=-g(n,\cdot)$ and decompose any spacetime covector as $\zeta=\zeta(n)\theta^0+\zeta_\perp$, where $\zeta_\perp(n)=0$ and $|\zeta_\perp|_h$ is its spatial norm. The spatial principal block is the linear map on $\mathbb R^3\oplus\mathbb R^3$ defined by $S(\xi)(u,v)=(-C(\xi)v,C(\xi)u)$. It is real symmetric, has eigenvalues $0,0,|\xi|,|\xi|,-|\xi|,-|\xi|$, and satisfies $\|S(\xi)\|=|\xi|$. Therefore the principal symbol $P(\zeta)=\zeta(n)I_6+S(\zeta_\perp)$ is positive definite for every covector with $\zeta(n)>|\zeta_\perp|_h$. In the adapted coordinates its time matrix is $\alpha^{-1}I_6$, and every coordinate spatial matrix is symmetric. Derivatives of the frame and metric enter only as smooth lower-order coefficients depending on $(g,g^{-1},\partial g,e,b)$; in a first-order metric state they are zero-order terms. The remaining two Maxwell equations are the constraints $\operatorname{div}_h e=0$ and $\operatorname{div}_h b=0$.

Let $F$ be a smooth real two-form on a smooth oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with the connection, Hodge star, and tensor $Q_{ab}=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\tfrac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}$ of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]]. For a smooth vector field $J$, suppose

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0J^b.$$

Then $Q_{ab}$ is symmetric and trace-free, and the SI-normalized stress tensor $T^{\rm EM}_{ab}=\mu_0^{-1}Q_{ab}$ satisfies

$$\nabla^aT^{\rm EM}_{ab}=-F_{bc}J^c.$$

In the source-free case $J=0$, $\nabla^aT^{\rm EM}_{ab}=0$. If $n$ is a future unit normal and $(\mathfrak e_1,\mathfrak e_2,\mathfrak e_3)$ a positively oriented orthonormal spatial triad, put $e_i:=F(\mathfrak e_i,n)$, $b_i:=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathfrak e_j,\mathfrak e_k)$, and $(e\times b)_i:=\epsilon_{ijk}e_jb_k$. Then

$$T^{\rm EM}(n,n)=\frac{|e|^2+|b|^2}{2\mu_0},\qquad T^{\rm EM}(n,\mathfrak e_i)=-\frac{(e\times b)_i}{\mu_0}.$$

These are pointwise tensor identities. In the SI interpretation $e=E/c$ and $b=B$ have units tesla; no measurement or physical applicability claim is included.

Let $u$ be a smooth future-directed vector field with $g(u,u)=-1$, and let $Z:M\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth scalar with units coulomb, interpreted within this model as charge per number-density unit. Define the current and matter stress by

$$j^a=cN(\epsilon)Z u^a,\qquad T_{m,ab}=(\epsilon+p(\epsilon))u_a u_b+p(\epsilon)g_{ab}.$$

$$\nabla^aT_{m,ab}=F_{bc}j^c,\qquad u^a\nabla_aZ=0,$$

Let $M^n$ be an oriented smooth manifold without boundary. $$\mathcal I_M(\omega)=\sum_i I_{\phi_i}(\chi_i\omega)\quad(K=\operatorname{supp}\omega),$$
using the signed chart integrals. This value is independent of the finite functions and charts. It defines a linear functional, is local under restriction to an open set containing the support, and for $n\ge1$ satisfies

Assume Countable Choice for the enthalpy integral. Let smooth fields satisfy [[def-emg-strict-charged-barotropic-system]], with $\epsilon\in J$, $u$ future unit timelike, and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$. Put $c_s=\sqrt{p'(\epsilon)}$ and use the enthalpy coordinate

$$r(\epsilon)=\int_{\epsilon_*}^{\epsilon}\frac{\sqrt{p'(z)}}{z+p(z)}\,dz.$$

On a local chart with a smooth frame $e_1,e_2,e_3$ for the positive-definite subbundle $u^\perp$, the energy and momentum equations are equivalent to

$$u^a\nabla_a r+c_s\nabla_a u^a=0,\qquad u^a\nabla_a u_b+c_s(\delta_b{}^a+u_bu^a)\nabla_a r=\frac{F_{bc}j^c}{\epsilon+p},\qquad u^a\nabla_aZ=0.$$

$$Q_\zeta((a,v,z),(a',v',z'))=\zeta(u)\bigl(aa'+g(v,v')+zz'\bigr)+c_s\bigl(a\zeta(v')+a'\zeta(v)\bigr).$$

derivations.claim: The derivative of $p(\epsilon)=w\epsilon$ is $p'=w$. Since $w>0$ and $\epsilon>0$, $p'=w\in(0,1)$ and $\epsilon+p=(1+w)\epsilon>0$ on $J$. Thus the strict EOS hypotheses hold.

For every $z>0$, $(z+p(z))^{-1}=((1+w)z)^{-1}$. Substituting this in [F1] and integrating gives $N=N_*\exp((1+w)^{-1}\log(\epsilon/\epsilon_*))=N_*(\epsilon/\epsilon_*)^{1/(1+w)}$. The logarithm is dimensionless because both arguments are energy densities.

Since $\sqrt{p'(z)}=\sqrt w$, [F2] gives $r=(\sqrt w/(1+w))\log(\epsilon/\epsilon_*)$. Differentiating yields $r'=\sqrt w/((1+w)\epsilon)>0$, so $r$ is strictly increasing. As $\epsilon\downarrow0$ its logarithm tends to $-\infty$, and as $\epsilon\to\infty$ it tends to $+\infty$; the positive prefactor preserves these limits, so its range is all of $\mathbb R$. Solving the displayed formula gives $\epsilon/\epsilon_*=\exp((1+w)r/\sqrt w)$; inserting this in step 2.1 yields $N=N_*e^{r/\sqrt w}$.

Let $\Sigma$ be a compact oriented smooth three-manifold without boundary with smooth Riemannian metric $h$. Let $n$ be a future unit normal, let $e$ be the electric vector determined by the two-form convention of [[def-emg-strict-charged-barotropic-system]], and suppose smooth initial data for that system satisfy the sourced electric Gauss constraint

$$\operatorname{div}_h e=-\mu_0 g(j,n).$$

Define the SI normal-charge integral

$$Q_n:=-\frac1c\int_\Sigma g(j,n)\,\operatorname{vol}_h=\int_\Sigma N Z\bigl(-g(u,n)\bigr)\,\operatorname{vol}_h.$$

Then $Q_n=0$. The result is conditional on the stated Gauss constraint; it does not assert existence of initial data satisfying the remaining Einstein or magnetic constraints.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, and let $n$ be an observer at $p$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). Write $h:=h_n$,
$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,n)=0\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]) and
$\mathbb Rn=\{\lambda n:\lambda\in\mathbb R\}$. Then:

1. $h:T_pM\to T_pM$ is linear, $h(n)=0$, $h(v)=v$ for every $v\in n^{\perp}$
   and $h\circ h=h$; its kernel is $\ker h=\mathbb Rn$, its image is
   $\operatorname{im}h=n^{\perp}$, and
   $T_pM=\mathbb Rn\oplus n^{\perp}$ is an orthogonal direct sum: every
   $v\in T_pM$ has the unique decomposition

   $$v=-g_p(v,n)\,n+h(v),$$

   in which $-g_p(v,n)n\in\mathbb Rn$ and $h(v)\in n^{\perp}$.
2. For all $v,w\in T_pM$ the **projection identity**

   $$g_p(h(v),h(w))=g_p(v,w)+g_p(v,n)g_p(n,w)$$

   holds; in particular $g_p(h(v),h(v))=g_p(v,v)+g_p(v,n)^2$.
3. $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive
   definite.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Write
$N_p^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,N_p)=0\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]) and let $T_p$ be the
timelike set, with components $C_p^+$ (the one containing $N_p$) and $C_p^-$,
and with future and past causality as fixed in
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]] and
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Then:

1. $N_p^{\perp}$ is a $3$-dimensional linear subspace of $T_pM$, and $g_p$ is
   positive definite on it; equivalently, every nonzero $v\in T_pM$ with
   $g_p(v,N_p)=0$ is spacelike.
2. $g_p(v,N_p)\neq0$ for every nonzero causal $v\in T_pM$.
3. $C_p^+=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\text{ and }g_p(v,N_p)<0\}$, and
   $C_p^-=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\text{ and }g_p(v,N_p)>0\}$.
4. A nonzero $v\in T_pM$ is causal and future-directed if and only if
   $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)$, and causal and past-directed if and only if
   $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C_p^-)$. Consequently
   $\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$ is exactly the set of
   future-directed causal vectors and $\operatorname{cl}(C_p^-)\setminus\{0\}$
   exactly the set of past-directed causal vectors,
   $\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\cap\operatorname{cl}(C_p^-)=\{0\}$, and every
   nonzero causal vector is exactly one of future-directed and past-directed.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and let
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an $\eta$-orthonormal ordered basis. Write
$v=v^0e_0+v^1e_1+v^2e_2+v^3e_3$ for the coordinates of $v$
([[thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis]]) and

$$\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert:=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2}.$$

Then $\eta(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert^2$, and the timelike set
$T:=\{v\in V:\eta(v,v)<0\}$ satisfies

$$T=T_+\cup T_-,\qquad T_+:=\{v:v^0>\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\},\qquad T_-:=\{v:v^0<-\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\}.$$

The sets $T_+$ and $T_-$ are nonempty, disjoint, open in $V$ (for the metric
topology of the distance $d(u,w):=\lVert c(u)-c(w)\rVert_2$ induced by the
coordinates $c(v):=(v^0,v^1,v^2,v^3)$), convex and path-connected, and they are
exactly the two connected components of $T$. In every $\eta$-orthonormal
ordered basis the two displayed coordinate sets coincide with the two
components of $T$ in some order, and they may be interchanged relative to a
previously fixed naming of the components. Moreover

$$\operatorname{cl}(T_+)=\{v:v^0\ge\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(T_-)=\{v:v^0\le-\lvert v_{\mathrm{vec}}\rvert\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(T_+)\cap\operatorname{cl}(T_-)=\{0\}.$$

$\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ for all $a,b$. Such a basis
is called **$\eta$-orthonormal**; in every $\eta$-orthonormal ordered basis
exactly one basis vector is timelike and the other three are spacelike, and the
count is the inertia $(3,1,0)$ of $\eta$.

For vectors $u,v$ in a real or complex inner product space,

$$|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\lVert u\rVert\lVert v\rVert.$$

Equality holds if and only if $u$ and $v$ are linearly dependent, including the case in which either vector is zero.

At a point choose an orthonormal basis by [F6], and choose its time vector in the future component; [F4] fixes that component by the time-orientation field and [F5] gives its coordinate form. Therefore the future unit vectors $u_0$ and $n$ have coordinates $u_0^0>|u_{0,\mathrm{vec}}|$ and $n^0>|n_{\mathrm{vec}}|$. By [F7], $g(u_0,n)=-u_0^0n^0+u_{0,\mathrm{vec}}\cdot n_{\mathrm{vec}}\le-u_0^0n^0+|u_{0,\mathrm{vec}}||n_{\mathrm{vec}}|<0$.
